belief: “Kindness is a trap. If someone is gentle with me, they are getting ready to hurt me.”
belief_plain: Kindness is a trap. If someone is gentle with me, they are getting ready to hurt me
origins: If gentleness was once the doorway to harm, kindness itself starts to feel like bait. A soft voice, a favor, or patience can make your body brace. That reaction is understandable. The lie says every gentle person is getting ready to hurt you, so you must refuse care. Some people are unsafe, and you are allowed to be careful. Not every kind person is the person who hurt you. A counselor can help you tell the difference without shaming the alarm. If you are not safe right now, call 911. You can also call the National Domestic Violence Hotline at 1-800-799-7233. If a child is being hurt, call Childhelp at 1-800-422-4453. A counselor can help you at a pace that is safe. You do not have to do this alone, or all at once.
self: If they are nice, they want something.
I should reject help before it turns.
No one is kind unless they are planning harm.
I would rather be harsh than fooled.
Even God’s kindness is a trick.
replacement: Some kindness was misused, and that does not make all kindness a trap. I can go slowly, and I can receive care from safe people and from God.
